name: Men's physique division

lead: Men's physique is a competition category in which men appear in board shorts and are judged on a lean, athletic build, with broad shoulders, a narrow waist and balanced upper body rather than maximum size.
For people interested in looks, it defines a muscular but not extreme ideal, the V-taper, and many lifters train toward it.

paras: Competitors train for shoulder, back and arm width with a tight waist and lean conditioning, and prepare for contests with structured diets. Federation rules set shorts length and required poses. Forum users discuss it as a physique target.
Contest prep can involve long, strict calorie restriction, and some federations permit or do not test for drug use. Judging is subjective and varies by federation.

angle.text: The division gives a concrete look to train for, an upper body wide relative to the waist, in a mid-sized, lean build.

lead: Men's physique is a division of competitive bodybuilding, recognised by federations such as the IFBB and NPC, in which competitors wear board shorts and are judged on the V-taper: wide shoulders and a narrow waist, with muscularity and conditioning. It was introduced in the early 2010s as a lighter-muscled alternative to classic bodybuilding.

In looksmaxxing discussion it works as a physique template. Users on looksmax.org compare it with powerlifting for appeal to women and ask how a competition-level physique would change their overall rating.[1][2][3] Opinions in these threads differ, with some arguing face matters more than physique and others emphasising frame and waist width.[1][3]
No clinical studies of the division itself exist.

paras: Competitors wear board shorts rather than posing trunks, and the shorts are required to be loose and opaque in IFBB rules, with the upper body the focus of judging.

One looksmax.org thread asks whether a good physique matters as much as a good face for attracting women, and a reply argues the face signals genetic quality.[1] Another weighs powerlifting against men's physique for a build that appeals to women, with replies disagreeing.[2] A third asks how a competition-level physique would change a user's PSL rating and notes people with narrow waists have the most to gain.[3]

lore.intro: Forum users treat men's physique as a physique goal and debate how much it adds relative to facial attractiveness.[1][2]

claims.claim: A good physique cannot make up for an average face
People with narrow waists gain the most from a men's physique build

timeline.event: IFBB officially recognises men's physique as a discipline.
